prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In this steep downward-angled hallway view with a slatted door on the left, lockers in the upper-left background (roughly 1.5–2.0 m away), and a wooden floor below, the camera wearer holds a smartphone in their left hand at the bottom-left (0.3–0.4 m away) while a second person in dark scrubs stands in the upper-right facing the wearer at about 0.8–1.2 m distance (0.5–0.8 m beyond the phone). The standing person's head and upper shoulders are cropped out of the top-right edge so eye contact cannot be seen, while their torso and feet angle toward the camera wearer and stay within mutual arm's reach. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer's right hand enters the bottom center in frames 3–4 at ~0.3 m depth before dropping to the bottom edge in frame 5, while the standing person uncrosses their tattooed left arm and reaches their right hand forward and down in frame 5 to within ~0.4–0.5 m of the camera, hovering just above the top of the phone. The depth map clearly reveals the continuous 3D slant of the floor plane, the top-to-bottom foreshortening along the standing person's body, and the rapid decrease in depth of the reaching right hand in frame 5, which are harder to judge quantitatively from the RGB strip alone. However, the map is unreliable where the floor/wall corner behind the phone turns into a black void with an exaggeratedly far depth, where small held items (the cup in frame 1 and cloth in frames 1–4) merge into the standing person's torso depth, and in frame 5 where the camera wearer's phone and hand become dimmer than the standing person's upper chest despite being physically closer.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground silhouettes against the hallway scene: the camera wearer's left hand and smartphone at the bottom-left (0.3–0.4 m from the camera) and right hand in frames 3–4, separated by about 0.5–0.8 m from the standing person in the upper-right (0.8–1.2 m away) whose head is out of view above the top frame edge. In frame 1, it detects the cup held near the standing person's chest at ~0.8 m (within that person's reach), and across frames 1–5 it tracks the contour of the standing person's body as their right arm extends downward toward the top-right corner of the phone in frame 5, bringing the two people's hands within ~0.1–0.2 m of each other. It also captures how the camera wearer's thumb and fingers wrap around and partially occlude the lower edges of the phone in frames 1, 3, and 4, and how the standing person's legs are foreshortened below their torso. Compared to RGB alone, the masks sharply delineate the exact boundary between the reaching right hand and the top of the smartphone in frame 5 and separate the cup from the dark shirt in frame 1. However, the map is highly unreliable across time: it misclassifies the wooden floor as a "dining table" in frames 1 and 4 while omitting it in other frames, drops the camera wearer's hands entirely in frames 2 and 5, merges the smartphone into the "person" mask in frame 3, misses the lockers, door, and held cloth across all frames, and splits the standing person's left arm into a separate "person" instance in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is sparse against the black background, failing to detect any skeletons in frames 1 and 4 despite both the camera wearer's hands (0.3–0.4 m away at bottom-left) and the standing person's body (0.8–1.2 m away in the upper-right, facing the wearer with head out of frame) being clearly visible in RGB. In frame 2, a single magenta hand skeleton localizes the standing person's right hand at ~0.9 m distance near their waist as they hold a white object within their own reach. In frame 3, magenta keypoints capture the camera wearer's right hand at ~0.3 m reaching toward the smartphone screen, alongside a yellow body skeleton that erroneously connects keypoints near the wearer's hands to torso-like joints floating over the empty floor between the two people. In frame 5, three magenta hand clusters simultaneously pinpoint the camera wearer's left hand on the left edge of the phone (~0.35 m), the standing person's right hand hovering just above the top-right of the phone (~0.45 m, within arm's reach of both people), and the standing person's left hand down at their left hip (~1.0 m). Where present, these hand skeletons make the exact finger articulation of the wearer's pinching right hand in frame 3 and the 3D spatial triangle of the three hands during the frame 5 reach more explicit than in RGB, but the map is overall very unreliable due to missed detections in most frames and the hallucinated yellow body skeleton in frame 3.
